# Ordered source-header occurrences

Six cases reuse the unchanged creator and B08's independently defined structure mutations. Each source retains two mixed-case X-Project headers that are not rendered by this creator. Their order/raw values and absence of observed custom-field associations are checked without claiming they should have been rendered.

Distinct/identical variants deliberately repeat Subject, a singleton under RFC 5322. These are malformed archival-source probes, not legal duplicate-Subject examples. The creator selects the first Subject; the existing mandatory source/XMP comparison detects that its XMP Subject does not preserve the complete repeated source value. The exact MESSAGE_SUBJECT_XMP failure remains required in ordinary profiles. B09 does not repair or waive that creator/source-fidelity issue.

The five rendered fields per message independently establish ten observations. Distinct repeated subjects identify occurrence 1; identical subjects remain ambiguous; swapped content has no supported occurrence match and falls outside its declared message pages. ClassMap ownership must agree. Isolated originals remain optional, while all ten observed texts must survive without source evidence. Rule 107 remains partial WARN throughout. Full standard-tagged/untagged rendered-header enumeration and arbitrary occurrence/aggregation semantics remain open.
